topic: Empirical Superiority of Rating Count over Bayesian Weighted Average in Top-N
problem_statement: Should unpersonalized popularity baseline rank movies by pure interaction count or by Bayesian/IMDb weighted average rating?
solution_or_decision: Select POPULARITY_COUNT as the primary baseline for MoodGraph. On 109,779 positive validation targets, POPULARITY_COUNT achieves NDCG@10 = 0.02789 and HR@10 = 5.519%, dramatically outperforming POPULARITY_WEIGHTED (NDCG@10 = 0.00771, HR@10 = 1.969%).
evidence: Real evaluation of all 109,779 positive validation users: Count HR@10=5.52% vs Weighted HR@10=1.97% (nearly 3x higher). NDCG@10=0.0279 vs 0.0077 (3.6x higher).
root_cause: MovieLens has severe popularity bias. High-average niche movies (v ~ 1,000, R ~ 4.48) outscore blockbusters in Bayesian average but only appeal to a tiny fraction (< 1%) of users, causing low HitRate and NDCG across the general population.
